$comment: RAY-CLOUD shared contract 1.0.0-draft.2. CLI verb map, result envelope and exit codes. Codes and their exit classes are in error-codes.json.

output.rule: A new verb writes exactly one final JSON envelope to stdout, with or without --json; progress and logs go to stderr. An existing verb without --json keeps its current output byte for byte. An existing verb with --json writes the envelope with its legacy result object unchanged in data and adds the warning RAY_W_LEGACY_OUTPUT; its legacy string errors become errors with code RAY_CHECK_FAILED and the string as message, and its spec errors become SPEC_ codes.
output.secrets: No output, log, error message or envelope field ever carries a secret value, a bindings-file value, an identity or key file content, or a path component known to be secret.
output.operationId: A CLI verb generates a fresh random UUID v4 operationId per invocation, prints it on stderr and records it in any receipt. A runtime.<name> result echoes the operationId of its request, which the caller chose and reuses on retry (runtime-control.md "Common shapes").
output.interrupt: On SIGINT or SIGTERM a verb stops at a safe point, leaves any fence it took in place, writes an envelope with RAY_INTERRUPTED and a recovery instruction, and exits 6.

exitCodes.existingVerbs: Existing verbs keep 0, 1 and 2 for every outcome they have today. An unexpected internal error, which exits 2 today (packages/app/cli/src/index.ts:597-611), exits 7 from this release. Codes 3 to 6 appear on an existing verb only for an outcome that verb does not have today, such as RAY_LOCK_TIMEOUT when the boot waits on the shared advisory lock.

globalFlags.description: Accepted on every verb. New verbs always write the envelope; the flag is accepted for symmetry.

deployDispatch.rule: rayspec deploy <path> selects the bundle path when the file starts with the ZIP signature 50 4B 03 04 or 50 4B 05 06, or when the path ends in .ray (ASCII case-insensitive). The check reads at most the first 4 bytes and runs before any configuration is loaded or any database connection is opened. A .ray path whose bytes are not a ZIP is refused with RAY_INVALID_ARCHIVE reason not-a-zip. Every other file takes the legacy YAML path.
deployDispatch.legacyOrder: The legacy YAML path validates the spec and signer key before applying the platform migration chain. This is a fix of today's order (the chain is applied at packages/app/server/src/composition-root.ts:1925 before the spec is parsed at :2041); a spec that fails validation now leaves the database untouched, and the exit code stays 1.

readerPipeline.governedBy: 01-RAY-BUNDLE.md "Reader pipeline" fixes the order of its numbered items 1 to 17 and the reason of each failure; this table repeats them as reader steps with the codes each can emit. Where a verb pipeline lists reader steps it runs them in this order, and on any disagreement 01-RAY-BUNDLE.md governs.

verbs.orderRule: No database connection is opened and no configuration is loaded until the archive, manifest, spec, bindings and signer key have validated. No database mutation happens until the plan is accepted. The shared advisory lock is held for every schema mutation.
verbs.jsonRule: With --json, stdout carries exactly one envelope, written when the process refuses or stops; banners and logs go to stderr.
